Sieving, the stack drawn see-through: 3-D throwing motion, amplitude 0.2-3 mm (Retsch). Each size class falls until a cloth stops it. Al powder under 63 um is among the most ignitable metal dusts: the bench wants bonding, grounding and extraction (DAL's sieve note).

The fractions, by the sieve that keeps each. The LPBF cut, 20-63 um, is the No. 325 and the pan: there is no 20 um sieve, and DAL found under 20 um is about 0.05 % by mass.
Taking the stack apart is left to a person, in a respirator, under extraction: the cut is the finest, most ignitable powder of the run. The No. 325's and the pan's powder go into a jar.

To the Aconity MIDI, 4.8 m along the line, past the VLM's opening.

The door opens, and the chamber is drawn see-through. The MIDI's 170 mm build cylinder is at the front; the 170 mm powder supply cylinder is behind it (DAL PR #169). Its piston drops to take the powder.

The arm carries the jar in, level, over the supply cylinder, and turns its wrist to pour. One run's cut is tens of grams; a 30 mm build in a 170 mm cylinder takes about 1 kg in the bed, so in practice the supply is topped up from many runs, or a smaller build cylinder is fitted.

The print, sped up and cut open: the recoater spreads a layer from the supply over the build cylinder, the laser melts the bars' and the lug's outlines, the platform drops one layer. 600 layers of 50 um (assumed) make the 30 mm build.
